name: Taphath
title: Solomon's daughter and wife of Ben-Abinadab
summary: Taphath was a daughter of King Solomon. She was given as a wife to Ben-Abinadab, one of Solomon's twelve district governors responsible for supplying the king's household. Her marriage was likely a political arrangement to strengthen loyalty between the royal house and the administrative leaders of the kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Solomon's daughter
keyEvents.description: Taphath is mentioned as a daughter of King Solomon in connection with the listing of his twelve district governors. She was married to Ben-Abinadab, who ruled over the entire region of Dor.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's administrative system
keyEvents.description: Taphath's marriage was part of Solomon's strategy to organize and consolidate his kingdom through twelve administrative districts, where each governor had to provide for the king's household one month each year.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's wealth and power
keyEvents.description: The context surrounding Taphath's marriage illustrates Solomon's immense wealth and political power, as his daughters were used in strategic alliances with his own officials.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's Royal Family
keyEvents.description: Solomon had many wives and children, and Tahath was among the royal daughters who were married off to ensure political stability in the kingdom.
